statement: You are given an undirected graph: a vertex count n (vertices numbered 0 to n − 1) and a list of edges [u, v].

Store it as an adjacency list, the way it is usually written in C++: a vector<int> adj[n], one vector per vertex. For each edge [u, v], in list order, push v onto adj[u] and u onto adj[v], so that every undirected edge is stored twice.

examples.explanation: Vertex 1 appears in the edges 0 − 1, 1 − 2 and 1 − 3, so its list is [0, 2, 3]. The 5 edges give 10 entries in total.
Each list keeps the order its edges were read in. Vertex 5 is met in 4 − 5, then 3 − 5, then 0 − 5, so its list is [4, 3, 0].
